title: MicroZig to Adopt Strict No LLM / No AI Policy
content:
This is largely taken from Zig's Code of Conduct.
The rules here are strict. This space is for focused, on topic, technical work on the MicroZig and Zig Embedded Group projects only. It is everyone’s responsibility to maintain a positive environment, especially when disagreements occur.
This document applies to the Zig Embedded Group GitHub organization and Discord server.
This policy takes effect October 28th, 2026.
No LLM-generated content, whether it be code or prose.
No paraphrasing LLM-generated content.
No LLMs for editing, including fixing spelling or grammatical errors.
No LLMs for translation. English is encouraged, but not required. You are welcome to post in your native language and rely on others to have their own translation tools of choice to interpret your words.
No LLMs for brainstorming and then sharing the results of that brainstorming, even if you create the prose. If you use a chatbot to give you advice on a comment on the issue tracker, that comment is unwelcome.
No LLMs for finding bugs.
No talking about use of chatbot/LLM services.
Examples of behavior that contribute to creating a positive environment include:
- Using welcoming and inclusive language.
- Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences.
- Gracefully accepting constructive criticism.
- Helping another person accomplish their own goals.
- Showing empathy towards others.
- Showing appreciation for others’ work.
- Validating someone else’s experience, skills, insight, and use cases.
Examples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:
- Unwelcome sexual attention or advances, or use of sexualized language or imagery that causes discomfort.
- Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal attacks. Anything antagonistic towards someone else.
- Off-topic discussion of any kind - especially offensive or sensitive issues.
- Publishing others’ private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission.
- Discussing this Code of Conduct or publicly accusing someone of violating it.
- Making someone else feel like an outsider or implying a lack of technical abilities.
- Destructive behavior. Anything that harms MicroZig or another open-source project.
If you need to report an issue you can contact Matthew Knight and Felix Queißner. We will swiftly remove anyone who is antagonizing others or being generally destructive.
This includes Private Harassment. If person A is directly harassed or antagonized by person B, person B will be blocked from participating in this space even if the harassment didn’t take place on one of the mediums directly under rule of this Code of Conduct.
As noted, discussing this Code of Conduct should not take place on GitHub, or Discord, because these spaces are for directly working on code, not for meta-discussion. If you have any issues with it, you can contact me directly, or you can join one of the community spaces that has different rules.
Matthew Knight mattnite@proton.me
Thanks for reading the rules. Together, we can make this space welcoming and inclusive for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

report.summary: MicroZig's Zig Embedded Group bans all LLM-generated code, prose, editing, translation, and even discussion of AI use in its GitHub and Discord spaces, effective October 28, 2026.
report.background: MicroZig is a hardware abstraction layer for embedded development in Zig, maintained by the volunteer-run Zig Embedded Group. Its new Code of Conduct, adapted from Zig's own CoC, arrives as open-source projects struggle with a flood of low-quality AI-generated pull requests and issue comments — so-called "AI slop" — that shift review burden onto unpaid maintainers. Similar debates have roiled curl, NetBSD, Gentoo, the Linux kernel, and QEMU, where policies range from outright bans to mandatory disclosure. Zig itself has taken a skeptical public stance on LLM-assisted contributions. The MicroZig policy is unusually strict: it forbids not only AI-written code and prose but also LLM-assisted spellchecking, translation, brainstorming, and bug-hunting, plus any public discussion of chatbot use. The delayed effective date of October 28, 2026 signals a grace period before enforcement begins.
key_points: Blanket ban on AI output: no LLM-generated code or prose, no paraphrasing of AI text, and no using chatbots for editing, spellchecking, or translation. Posts in a contributor's native language are explicitly welcome instead, with readers expected to bring their own translation tools.

Brainstorming counts as contamination: if a contributor asks a chatbot for advice and then writes a comment themselves, that comment is still unwelcome. This closes the common loophole of 'I only used it to think.'

Discussion of AI use is itself off-topic: mentioning chatbot or LLM services in GitHub issues or Discord is prohibited, alongside other meta-discussion such as debating the Code of Conduct itself in those channels.

Enforcement is broad and maintainer-driven: the two named maintainers, Matthew Knight and Felix Queißner, can remove participants for antagonism or destructive behavior, including private harassment that occurs outside the moderated platforms.
report.impact: The policy pushes the open-source AI debate from disclosure toward prohibition. For the AI industry, it signals that a segment of the developer community treats LLM involvement as a trust and quality problem, not a productivity feature — a data point that matters as coding assistants chase embedded and systems-programming markets. For developers, it means tooling choices become conduct issues: an assistant used to fix a typo in a PR description could be a violation. For regular users of embedded software, stricter review may mean fewer low-effort patches and better-maintained firmware, at the cost of a higher barrier for newcomers and non-native English speakers. Watch whether other small projects copy the template.
report.tools: To follow along, read the CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md in the ZigEmbeddedGroup/microzig repository and Zig's own Code of Conduct for comparison. If you want to contribute, install the Zig toolchain and explore MicroZig's HAL for embedded targets. For AI-policy precedents, track curl's and NetBSD's contribution guidelines and the growing community lists of project AI policies. Rust's Embassy and Zephyr are worth watching as embedded frameworks with contrasting AI stances.
